cases.evidence: Probe (puppeteer, scripted): click #open-modal -> focus on button#dlg-x; press Escape -> scrimShown=false and focus is on button#open-modal ('Verify your identity'). Davin's claim is exactly right: focus returns to the opener button, NOT to <body>. result.json's mechanism for this case claims 'closeConfirm() ... omits confirmOpener.focus(), so dismissing the confirm modal collapses focus to <body>; the base-layer focusin guard then yanks focus to #zip'. grep: no #confirm, closeConfirm, confirmOpener, #zip, 'Get a quote' or 'Discard this quote' anywhere in case-06.html, and primarySelector 'div#confirm[role="dialog"]' matches nothing. The page's real defect (which I also verified, and which case-06.md describes correctly) is an F10 trap in the embedded frame: from inside the widget, 14 consecutive Tabs cycle dl -> dob -> rescan -> submit -> dl ... forever, and Escape there leaves scrimShown=true with focus still on #dob, because the Escape listener is bound on the parent document.
cases.reasoning: The complaint is specific and verified: the metadata narrates a two-stacked-modal insurance wizard that does not exist, and its stated Esc->body behaviour is contradicted by the page (Esc -> opener). This is the 'metadata copy-pasted from a different case' pattern, and the repair is mechanical because case-06.md already documents the shipped page correctly and my probe confirms it. expected='failed' is unchanged - the page really is a keyboard trap - so no ground-truth flip is involved. edits.oldString: "scenario": "Insurance quote wizard with two STACKED modals. The base 'Get a quote' modal is conformant in isolation (Esc closes, Close in cycle, focus restore). From inside it the user opens a top 'Discard this quote?' confirmation modal. The defect is the nested-dismiss handoff: pressing Esc on the top modal closes it but drops focus to <body> (it omits the focus-restore call), and the still-armed base trap re-grabs the next Tab, snapping focus back to the base modal's first field — a re-trap instead of an orderly return.",
edits.newString: "scenario": "Cobalt Bank account-opening flow with ONE modal that is conformant containment in isolation: 'Verify your identity' opens a role=dialog aria-modal=true overlay, initial focus lands on a real focusable Close button, an Escape handler on the parent document closes it, Close/Cancel/Continue sit in the Tab cycle, and focus is restored to the opener. The defect is the embedded third-party format in the modal body: a 'SecureScan' KYC widget delivered as an <iframe srcdoc> second document whose own Tab-wrap and focusin re-grab keep focus circulating inside the frame forever, while the modal's Escape listener - living one document up - never receives keydowns fired inside the frame. A keyboard user can enter the verification step but cannot leave it.",

edits.oldString: "mechanism": "Broken focus handoff across stacked layers: closeConfirm() removes the top scrim but omits confirmOpener.focus(), so dismissing the confirm modal collapses focus to <body>; the base-layer focusin guard then yanks focus to #zip on the next Tab (verified: Esc->body, Tab->#zip). The keyboard user cannot return in an orderly way to where they were and is re-trapped in the base modal — the exit from the stack is broken even though each modal is escapable alone.",
edits.newString: "mechanism": "Keyboard trap at a format seam (WCAG F10): once Tab moves focus into iframe#kyc, the widget's own keydown handler wraps last->first / first->last and a focusin listener re-grabs any focus that reaches the frame's body, so neither Tab nor Shift+Tab can carry focus back out to the parent modal; the parent document's Escape-to-close listener never fires because the keydown is dispatched in the child document. Verified by probe: from inside the widget, 14 consecutive Tabs cycle dl -> dob -> rescan -> submit -> dl ... indefinitely, and Escape leaves the scrim open (scrimShown: true) with focus still on #dob. Escape pressed while focus is still on a PARENT-document control does close the dialog and restores focus to #open-modal, which is why the outer modal looks conformant when tested alone.",

edits.oldString: "whyAutomatedToolsMiss": "Both dialogs are textbook-valid in isolation: real role=dialog aria-modal=true overlays, accessible names, focusable Close buttons, wired Esc handlers — every static check passes, and even a keyboard test of each dialog separately finds Esc and Close working. The failure exists only in the stack transition (open-confirm-from-base -> Esc-confirm -> focus-to-body -> Tab -> base re-trap), requiring multi-step, stateful keyboard reasoning about focus handoff between layers across time, which scanners do not perform. There is no missing attribute; the bug is an omitted focus-restore call whose effect manifests only dynamically.",
edits.newString: "whyAutomatedToolsMiss": "Every static signal is clean: a real role=dialog aria-modal=true overlay with an accessible name (aria-labelledby), a focusable Close button, a wired Escape handler, and an <iframe> that carries a title attribute - axe / IBM / WAVE have nothing to report, and even a keyboard test of the outer modal's own controls passes (Esc closes it and restores focus to the opener). The failure appears only when the tester crosses the document boundary into the embedded widget and finds that Tab, Shift+Tab and Esc all fail to bring focus back out. Automated tools do not drive the keyboard across frame boundaries or reason about which document a key listener is bound to, and no attribute is missing for a scanner to flag.",
